skill.description: Advanced AgentDB guidance for QUIC synchronization, hybrid vector search, custom distance metrics, multi-database layouts, and production operations.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, sample private IP addresses, and example database paths. I confirmed user-directed shell command examples and the sudo firewall command because they can affect the host if copied. Additional semantic risk comes from unpinned npx @latest usage and incomplete trust-boundary guidance for QUIC sync.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo ufw allow 4433/udp with guidance that requires explicit user approval and source-restricted firewall rules.
Pin AgentDB CLI versions and tell users to verify package provenance before running npx commands.
Add clear guidance for trusted peers, firewall source restrictions, authentication expectations, and non-production example addresses.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External CLI Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs users to run npx agentdb@latest in multiple examples. Pulling the latest package at runtime can execute unexpected code if the package or registry is compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly use npx with @latest, so the supply-chain concern is directly evidenced. The risk depends on user execution, so severity is medium rather than critical.

semantic_findings.title: Broad QUIC Sync Exposure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill shows QUIC sync peers and a firewall rule without clear trust-boundary guidance. Users could expose the sync service more broadly than intended.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples clearly enable QUIC peers and open UDP port 4433, but the file does not specify authentication or source-limited firewall rules in the shown guidance.

content.value_statement: Advanced AgentDB projects need reliable sync, search, and database operations. This skill guides QUIC sync, hybrid search, metrics, sharding, and production commands.
actual_capabilities: Explains QUIC synchronization setup for AgentDB peers.
Shows cosine, Euclidean, dot product, and custom metric patterns.
Describes hybrid vector search with metadata filters and weights.
Covers multiple database adapters and shard routing examples.
Outlines MMR, context synthesis, pooling, logging, and error handling.
Lists CLI operations for import, export, merge, vacuum, analyze, and reindex workflows.
limitations: Does not include a runnable AgentDB project or test fixture.
Uses example IP addresses, paths, and domains that need local replacement.
Does not verify AgentDB version compatibility at runtime.
Includes shell commands that require user review before execution.

use_cases.title: Plan Distributed AgentDB Sync
use_cases.description: Map peer configuration, ports, and deployment steps for QUIC synchronization across AgentDB nodes.

use_cases.title: Design Hybrid Retrieval
use_cases.description: Choose metadata filters, vector metrics, weighting, and MMR settings for retrieval-heavy applications.

use_cases.title: Operate AgentDB Databases
use_cases.description: Review import, export, merge, vacuum, analyze, logging, and recovery workflows for production use.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Distance Metric
prompt_templates.prompt: I am storing these embedding types in AgentDB: [describe data]. Recommend a distance metric and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Hybrid Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AgentDB hybrid search plan for [domain]. Include filters, weighting, result count, and MMR settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Database Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB domains: [list domains]. Propose database separation, shard keys, and operational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit QUIC Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this AgentDB QUIC sync plan: [paste plan]. Identify peer trust, firewall, retry, monitoring, and rollout concerns.

output_examples.input: Which metric should I use for text embeddings?
output_examples.output: Use cosine similarity for normalized text embeddings. It focuses on semantic direction and is the default general-purpose choice.

output_examples.input: I need product search with category and rating filters.
output: Use hybrid search with vector similarity for meaning and metadata filters for category, price, stock, and rating.
Start with higher vector weight, then tune metadata weight after measuring relevance.

output_examples.input: How should I prepare QUIC sync for production?
output_examples.output: Define trusted peers, restrict firewall sources, monitor latency, test retry behavior, and avoid copying example addresses unchanged.

best_practices: Replace all example paths, IP addresses, and hostnames before use.
Pin CLI versions and review commands before running them.
Test retrieval quality and latency before enabling production sync.
anti_patterns: Do not expose QUIC sync ports to untrusted networks.
Do not use one database for unrelated high-volume domains without a sharding plan.
Do not rely on default metric settings without validating retrieval quality.

faq.question: Does this skill install AgentDB?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for AgentDB features. Users must install and verify dependencies separately.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is Markdown documentation, but it includes commands that users may choose to run.

faq.question: Are the IP addresses production-ready?
faq.answer: No. They are private-network examples. Replace them with trusted peers and restrict firewall access.

faq.question: What retrieval features are covered?
faq.answer: It covers distance metrics, hybrid metadata filtering, weighted scoring, MMR diversity, and context synthesis.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Review privileged commands, unpinned npx examples, firewall guidance, and version compatibility notes.
